title: Short copy: brochure, flyer, menu, bio or listing
summary: Finished copy for one short piece: a brochure, flyer, mailer, sign, pack, sell sheet, menu or service list, press kit, bio, profile, listing or story.
deliverable: Copy written to the format and space you give, panel by panel, side by side or item by item: headline, body, proof, offer and call to action, with image, QR code or reply-tracking notes. Bios come in three lengths. Two headline options and a list of facts to confirm.

spec_fields.label: Which piece do you need?
options: Flyer, poster or direct mail postcard or letter
Shop signs: window, A-board, shelf and counter
Pack copy or unboxing insert cards
Menu, service menu or class list
Press kit or one-sheet (artist, release, speaker, podcast guest)

spec_fields.label: How many pieces?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers one, up to six per job. Each extra flyer, listing, story or product pack is one more. A menu or list of up to 30 items is one piece.

spec_fields.label: Size, panels or character limits
spec_fields.help: For example: tri-fold, 6 panels; A5 flyer; Instagram bio 150 characters; 250 words.

spec_fields.label: About your business
spec_fields.help: What you sell, who buys it and where you work.

spec_fields.label: The facts, items and prices to use
spec_fields.help: Dishes, services, rooms, products, dates, prices, contact details. Only these will be used.

spec_fields.label: What should readers do next?
spec_fields.help: Call, book, visit, order, scan the QR code.

spec_fields.label: Quotes, reviews or awards we may use
spec_fields.help: Only these will be quoted.

spec_fields.label: Tone and voice
spec_fields.help: A few words, or paste a sample of your writing.

rubric.text: Every piece and every item asked for is there, laid out the way the format works.
rubric.pass_rule: The draft has the number of pieces in the brief, labels each panel, side, section or item, and covers every dish, service, room, project or person the brief lists. Missing details are shown as [placeholders], not dropped.

rubric.text: Nothing is made up: every fact, price, name, quote or result comes from the brief.
rubric.pass_rule: No price, date, capacity, ingredient, award, credential, review, quote, client name or result appears unless it is in the brief. Any invented item fails this criterion.

rubric.text: The copy fits the size and limits given.
rubric.pass_rule: Where the brief gives a word count, character limit, panel count or size, each part stays within it and counts are shown for limited fields. Bios come in about 50, 150 and 400 words unless the brief asks for other lengths.

rubric.text: Each piece says who it is for, what is on offer and what to do next.
rubric.pass_rule: Each piece (not each menu item) names the subject or offer and its reader from the brief, ends with a call to action or contact line that matches the goal, and two headline or title options are given wherever the piece has a headline.

rubric.text: Short, plain sentences in the buyer's voice, with no filler.
rubric.pass_rule: Most sentences are under 20 words, there are no empty phrases such as 'world-class' or 'passionate about excellence', and the tone matches any voice notes or sample in the brief.

baseline_prompt: You are a copywriter for small businesses. Write the short piece described below (for example a brochure, flyer, postcard, shop sign set, pack copy, sell sheet, menu, press kit, bio, profile, listing or story). Lay it out the way the format works: panel by panel for a brochure, front and back for a postcard or pack, item by item for a menu or service list, section by section for a one-sheet or profile. Give a headline, body, proof and a clear call to action, and add short image or layout notes. Keep to any size or character limits and show counts. For bios, give about 50, 150 and 400 word versions. Offer two headline options. Use only the facts, prices and quotes I give and mark anything missing as a [placeholder]. End with a list of facts to confirm.
not_for: Design, layout or print-ready files
Invented reviews, awards, credentials, quotes or prices
Health, eco, safety or legal claims you cannot prove, or medical, legal or financial advice
Legal sign-off on food labels, allergens or packaging rules
Long brochures over 8 pages or whole websites (see the website page copy job)
Ads or emails (see the paid ads copy set and email jobs)
Posting to your profiles or listing sites, or logging in to them
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Tri-fold brochure (6 panels) for Harbourside Physio in Whitby. Services: sports massage, back pain clinic, post-surgery rehab. Sessions 45 minutes, 55 pounds. Open Monday to Saturday, 8am to 7pm, 14 Quay Street. Audience: adults 40 to 70 with aches and stiffness. Goal: call 01947 600 112 to book.

Menu descriptions for Little Fig, a 30-seat brunch cafe. 14 dishes and 6 drinks (list pasted with ingredients and prices). We bake our own sourdough and use eggs from Hollins Farm two miles away. Want each description under 20 words plus one header line about us. Warm, a bit cheeky.

Three bios for our folk duo The Marsh Hens: 50, 150 and 400 words, plus a one-line listing description. We formed in 2019 in Norwich, released two EPs (Low Tide 2021, Salt Roads 2024), played Cambridge Folk Festival 2025. Quotes from BBC Radio Norfolk we may use are pasted. Voice: plain, a little dry.

A5 flyer and a direct mail postcard for Greenleaf Lawn Care. Offer: first spring cut free when you book 10 cuts from 28 dollars each, areas 98101 to 98109 only, ends 30 April. Audience: homeowners with small yards. Add a QR code note and a way to track replies (use code SPRING10).

Airbnb listing title and description for our cabin 'Pine Hollow' near Asheville. Sleeps 4, 2 bedrooms, wood stove, hot tub, 12 minutes to downtown, gravel road (4x4 not needed). House rules: no parties, no pets, quiet after 10pm. Title max 50 characters.

LinkedIn profile rewrite for me, Priya Nair, a freelance payroll consultant for UK firms with 10 to 80 staff. 11 years at two payroll bureaus, CIPP qualified. Goal: get enquiries from finance managers. Need headline (220 characters max), about section and experience bullets. Current profile pasted.

demand_sources.note: Talo's brochure cost guide says professional writers charge $200 to $500 to write the copy for a flyer or brochure, since most firms write their own.
Copywriting rate guide lists brochure or flyer copy at $300 to $1,500 a project, varying with page count and design work.

title: Weekly or monthly KPI report from your numbers
summary: A short report from the numbers you supply: what changed, why it matters and what to decide, for owners, boards, funders, landlords or clients.
deliverable: A one to two page report: a five-line summary; your key numbers against last period and target; a red, amber or green status and a plain comment on each; what moved and why; top risks; and three actions or decisions. Adds a simple forecast, agenda or board questions if you ask.

spec_fields.label: Which report do you need?
options: Board, partner or trustee finance pack
Financial health check or ratio sheet

spec_fields.label: Which period does it cover?
spec_fields.help: For example: October 2026, or the week of 3 November.

spec_fields.label: Your numbers
spec_fields.help: Paste figures or an export for this period and the last one. Add last year if you have it.

spec_fields.label: How many numbers to report on?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers up to 10.

spec_fields.label: What happened this period
spec_fields.help: Events, problems, launches, staff changes. We only give causes you tell us.

spec_fields.label: Who will read it?
spec_fields.help: Owner, board, partners, funder, landlord, client.

spec_fields.label: Anything to add?
options: A simple forecast for next period

spec_fields.label: Your template or headings
spec_fields.help: Paste it if a funder, board or client needs a set layout.

rubric.text: Every figure comes from the brief or is worked out from it, and the sums are right.
rubric.pass_rule: Each number appears in the brief or is a sum, difference, percentage or ratio of numbers in it. Recompute three changes against last period; they match. No target, benchmark or industry average appears unless the brief gives it.

rubric.text: It is the report type asked for, for the period and readers named.
rubric.pass_rule: The title names the period and report type; the report covers the numbers the brief marks as key, each shown with this period, last period and target when given; any extras ticked in the brief are included.

rubric.text: Each key number has a status and a plain comment on what moved and why.
rubric.pass_rule: Each key number has red, amber or green with the rule used (for example below target) and a one or two sentence comment. Causes come from the brief's notes or are labelled as possible causes to check.

rubric.text: It ends with the top risks and three actions or decisions tied to the numbers.
rubric.pass_rule: There are three actions or decisions (or the number asked for), each naming the number it addresses and an owner or next step, plus up to three risks drawn from the figures or notes.

rubric.text: Short, plain and quick to read.
rubric.pass_rule: Opens with a summary of three to five lines; the main text is under about 900 words excluding tables; terms such as MRR, NPS or occupancy are explained on first use.

baseline_prompt: You are a business analyst who writes short reports for owners and boards. Turn the numbers below into a one to two page report for the period and readers I name. Start with a five-line summary. Then show each key number for this period, last period and target if I gave one, with the change, a red, amber or green status (say the rule you used) and a one or two sentence comment. Explain what moved and why, using only causes from my notes; mark other causes as possibilities to check. List the top risks and finish with three actions or decisions, each tied to a number. Use only my figures, check every sum, and do not add targets or benchmarks I did not give. Explain any abbreviation on first use. Not tax or investment advice.
not_for: Audited, reviewed or official financial statements
Tax, investment or other regulated financial advice
Invented targets, benchmarks or causes
Reports meant to mislead investors, lenders, funders or owners
Funder narrative reports written mostly as prose (see the grant application job)
Building a live dashboard (see the KPI and dashboard spec job)
Logging in to your accounting, sales, booking or support systems; paste or attach exports instead
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Monthly KPI report for October 2026 for the two owners of Copper Kettle Coffee (3 cafes). Numbers pasted: sales by cafe, transactions, average spend, staff cost %, waste %, for September and October, plus targets (staff cost under 32%, waste under 4%). Notes: Leeds cafe closed 4 days for a broken espresso machine.

Weekly marketing report for week of 3 November. Spend 1,240 dollars (target 1,200), leads 61 (last week 48, target 60), cost per lead, email list 3,880 (+112), webinar sign-ups 140. We changed the Meta ad image on Tuesday. Readers: me and my sales lead. Three actions please.

Board finance report for our charity, Riverside Food Share, for Q3. Income 84,300 pounds vs budget 90,000, spend 79,100 vs 81,500, cash 61,200, unrestricted reserves 38,000 (policy says 3 months of costs, about 27,000). Add the three questions the trustees should ask.

Monthly owner report for 22 Ashgrove Road, a 6-flat building I manage. October rent due 7,650 dollars, collected 6,900 (flat 4 paid 750 late on 9 Nov). Repairs: boiler service 320, gutter clean 180. Flat 2 vacant since 15 Oct, two viewings booked. Owner wants next steps too.

Support report for October for our SaaS. Tickets 1,214 (Sept 1,030), first reply median 3h10m (target 2h), repeat contacts 14%, top reasons pasted with counts (billing 312, login 201, export bug 188). The export bug shipped 2 Oct and was fixed 17 Oct. Reader: CEO.

Subscription revenue report for September and October. Export pasted with MRR start 41,200, new 3,900, expansion 1,150, contraction 600, churned 2,450 for October and the same lines for September. Explain MRR in plain words for our two investors and add a simple forecast for November.

demand_sources.note: Contra listing for monthly management reporting with KPI tracking, variance commentary and recommended actions, starting at $1,500 a month.
Fractional CFO guide: a board or lender package with a one-page KPI dashboard and a short narrative is a standard deliverable in a $2,000 to $5,000 a month retainer.

title: Weighted scorecard for options or a list
summary: Clear criteria with weights, then your options (sites, markets, ideas, channels, a tender) or your list (leads, accounts, investors, shows) scored and ranked.
deliverable: The criteria and weights with reasons; must-haves as pass or fail gates; every option or row scored with the reason and missing data flagged; tiers or a ranked list with cut-off rules and deadlines in date order when you give them; a recommended pick, runner-up and a cheap way to check the pick; and a blank sheet to score new items.

spec_fields.label: What are you scoring?
options: Leads, accounts or investors to score and tier
Scoring rules only, for a list I will score later
Markets or customer segments to target first
Bid or no-bid on one tender
Risks or assumptions in an idea

spec_fields.label: How many options or rows?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers up to 50. Up to 150 per job. A one-tender check counts as 1.

spec_fields.label: Your options or list
spec_fields.help: Paste the list or CSV with the facts you have about each. Remove personal emails and phone numbers.

spec_fields.label: What are you trying to decide?
spec_fields.help: The goal, budget and time frame.

spec_fields.label: Criteria you already use
spec_fields.help: We will add weights and reasons.

spec_fields.label: How should results be grouped?
spec_fields.help: For example A, B and C, or pitch, maybe and skip.

rubric.text: Clear criteria with weights that add up, each with a reason.
rubric.pass_rule: Lists 4 to 8 criteria, each with a weight and a one-line reason tied to the goal; weights add to 100 percent (or the stated total); must-haves from the brief are pass or fail gates, not weights.

rubric.text: Every option or row is scored and placed, with a reason.
rubric.pass_rule: The number of scored items equals the number in the brief; each has a score per criterion or a total, a short reason (or a reason code with a key for lists over 30 rows), and a tier or rank; rows missing key data are flagged, not guessed. For scoring rules only, the rules are tested on two examples.

rubric.text: Scores rest only on facts in the brief.
rubric.pass_rule: No fact about an option (size, price, audience, traffic, funding stage, foot traffic, rival) appears unless it is in the brief; where data is missing the score is marked unknown or neutral and the gap is named.

rubric.text: Totals add up and the pick follows from the scores.
rubric.pass_rule: Recompute three weighted totals; they match the weights and scores. Tier cut-offs are written as numbers. The pick and any runner-up are the top scorers, or the reason to differ is stated (for one option, a go or no-go against the cut-off), and a cheap check of the pick is given.

rubric.text: Plain words and a sheet the buyer can reuse.
rubric.pass_rule: Includes a blank scoring sheet with criteria, weights and a scale that says what each score means (for example 1 to 5), so a new item can be scored the same way; no unexplained jargon.

baseline_prompt: You are a business analyst. Build a weighted scorecard for the options or list below. First set 4 to 8 criteria that fit my goal, give each a weight (adding to 100 percent) and a one-line reason, and treat my must-haves as pass or fail gates. Then score every option or row on each criterion with a short reason, using only the facts I give; mark missing data as unknown instead of guessing. Show the weighted totals, sort the items into tiers with number cut-offs, and name a recommended pick, a runner-up and a cheap way to check the pick before I commit. Finish with a blank scoring sheet and a scale that says what each score means. Do not score people on protected traits. Not investment advice.
not_for: Scoring people by age, sex, race, religion, disability or other protected traits
Buying, scraping or enriching lists
Facts about options that you do not supply, such as live traffic or footfall data
Investment advice or picking stocks, funds or deals to invest in
Legal advice on tenders or contracts
Side-by-side tool or supplier quotes (see the vendor comparison job)
Logging in to your CRM or other tools; paste or attach the list instead
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: We make accounting software for vets. Score and tier our list of 140 vet practices (CSV pasted: practice, town, vets on staff, number of sites, current software, last contact). Must-have: 3 or more vets. Tiers A, B, C so our two reps know who to call first.

Pick the best of 4 sites for a second bakery. Facts pasted for each: rent, size, parking spaces, distance to our first shop, nearby schools and offices, rivals on the same street, lease length. Budget for rent is 3,500 dollars a month max. We sell mostly breakfast and lunch.

Score 9 product ideas for our pet supply shop: margin, cost to make, demand signals we have (search notes and customer asks pasted), risk and fit with our brand. Top three please and a cheap test for the winner.

Bid or no-bid on a council tender to run grounds maintenance for 14 schools, 3-year contract worth about 420,000 pounds. Tender summary pasted. We have 9 staff, 4 vans, and have done 2 school contracts before. Deadline 28 November. Our rule: no bid if it needs more than 2 new hires.

Score 60 podcasts we found for a guest spot for our founder (sheet pasted: show, topic, episodes, last episode date, guest style, rough audience if known). We sell HR software to firms of 50 to 500 staff. Group them into pitch now, pitch later, skip.

Investor criteria for our pre-seed raise of 600,000 dollars for a construction safety app, then score our list of 35 angels and funds (pasted with stage, cheque size, sectors, location, notes). We want UK or Ireland based, cheques of 25k to 150k.

demand_sources.note: SBA guide tells new owners to weigh customers, operating costs, zoning, taxes and incentives when they choose where to locate a business.
Agency service page selling custom lead scoring models that score leads on fit with the ideal customer profile so sales teams know who to call first.

title: Offer, package or referral programme design
summary: A clear offer, good-better-best packages, a membership or subscription, bundles, crowdfunding rewards, or a referral, affiliate, partner or VIP programme.
deliverable: Who it is for; what is and is not included; tiers or options with plain names and prices; limits, perks or rewards; rules and payout terms; the maths, with worked examples, showing each tier or reward makes money; a one-page terms summary; and page text or invite messages, launch steps and a test to run.

spec_fields.label: What do you want designed?
options: Entry, core and premium offer ladder
Pilot or trial offer for early customers

spec_fields.label: What you sell now
spec_fields.help: Products or services, current prices and what each includes.

spec_fields.label: Your costs and margins
spec_fields.help: Cost to deliver each item, fees, shipping, staff time. We check every tier makes money.

spec_fields.label: Who buys and what they want
What should this offer do?
spec_fields.help: For example: raise order value, fill quiet days, get 50 new customers.

spec_fields.label: What you can and cannot offer
spec_fields.help: Capacity, the biggest discount you allow, perks you can afford.

spec_fields.label: Rules you must follow
spec_fields.help: Platform rules, industry rules, partner terms.

spec_fields.label: Rival prices and offers you know
spec_fields.help: Only these will be used.

spec_fields.label: Where will you show it?
spec_fields.help: Website, pricing page, shop, sales calls, campaign page.

rubric.text: It designs the offer or programme chosen, for the buyers and goal in the brief.
rubric.pass_rule: Names who each tier or option is for using buyer types from the brief, says what each includes and does not include, and links the design to the stated goal.

rubric.text: The maths shows each tier, bundle or reward makes money using the buyer's costs.
rubric.pass_rule: For each tier, bundle, reward or commission the draft shows price, the costs from the brief and the margin. Recompute two lines; they match. For rewards and commissions the cost per new sale is shown, and any option that loses money is flagged.

rubric.text: No made-up costs, prices, rival offers, demand or results.
rubric.pass_rule: Every cost, price, fee rate and rival price is from the brief or clearly labelled as an assumption to confirm; no sign-up, conversion or uplift figure is stated as fact or promised.

rubric.text: Rules, limits and terms are spelled out.
rubric.pass_rule: Includes limits (caps, revisions, usage, payout timing, expiry, who qualifies) and a one-page plain terms summary; nothing is promised as unlimited beyond the capacity the brief gives.

rubric.text: Plain names and honest presentation.
rubric.pass_rule: Tier names and page text use plain words; no fake urgency, hidden fees, fake 'was' prices, or rewards that depend mainly on recruiting other recruiters.

baseline_prompt: You are an offer and pricing strategist for small businesses. Design the offer, package set or programme described below. Say who each option is for, what it includes and leaves out, and give plain names and prices. For programmes such as referral, affiliate, partner, VIP or crowdfunding rewards, set the rewards, who qualifies, limits, payout timing and fraud rules. Using only my costs, show the maths for each tier or reward: price, costs and margin, and the cost per new sale. Flag anything that loses money. Add a one-page plain terms summary, short page text, launch steps and one test to run. Use only facts I give; label anything assumed. No fake urgency, hidden fees or pyramid-style rewards. Not legal or tax advice.
not_for: Price-fixing with rivals, or deceptive pricing
Legal contracts, terms of service or partner agreements (you get a plain summary for your lawyer)
Tax, VAT or other regulated financial advice
Pyramid or misleading reward schemes
Rewards for reviews where platform rules or law ban them
Full research into rival prices (see the pricing research job)
Setting up the offer in your shop, billing or affiliate software, or logging in to it
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Good-better-best packages for my wedding photography. Now I sell one package at 2,400 dollars (8 hours, 400 photos, online gallery). Costs: second shooter 350, album 280 at cost, editing about 20 hours. Couples want smaller weekday options too. Goal: raise average booking to 2,800.

A refer-a-friend scheme for Spark Bright Cleaning. Average regular client pays 85 pounds a fortnight, gross margin 38%. We lose about 1 in 5 new clients in the first two months. Want rewards for both sides, limits, fraud rules and the ask messages after the third clean.

Membership offer for our climbing gym. Now day passes are 18 dollars and a 10-pass is 150. 1,100 visits a month, 60% weekday evenings. Staff cost per extra member is near zero, but we are full on Saturdays. Want one to three levels with limits and a check the numbers add up.

Affiliate programme for our 49 dollar online course on bookkeeping for freelancers. Course fee after payment fees: 46.80. Refund rate 6%. We want bloggers and accountants to promote it. Need commission rate with maths, cookie window, payout rules, approval rules and a one-page terms summary.

Bundles and add-ons for our candle shop. 12 scents, 3 sizes (costs and prices pasted). Average order 34 pounds, shipping costs us 4.20 per order. Free shipping over 40. Goal: get average order over 45. Need five bundles with price, margin, page text and where to show each.

Crowdfunding reward tiers for a foldable bike pannier. Unit cost 31 dollars at 1,000 units, 24 at 3,000. Platform fee 5% plus 3% card fees. Shipping US 9, EU 16. Target 60,000 dollars. Want 5 to 8 tiers with early bird limits and add-ons, all making money after fees.

demand_sources.note: Mercury's guide to pricing a consulting business explains flat, tiered and retainer packages and says each needs a clear scope, exclusions and payment terms.
Constant Contact survey of 854 consumer-facing small businesses, reported by Fox Business: 82% said new customers find them through referrals.

title: Plan for one deal, key account or negotiation
summary: A plan for one live deal, key account, renewal, at-risk customer, stuck case, or a negotiation with a buyer, supplier or lender, with the messages to send.
deliverable: The situation; who is involved, what each likely cares about, who sways whom and who you have not met; risks; your goal, walk-away point and what you can trade; their likely position; a dated action plan or shared close plan with owners; growth ideas for key accounts; and the messages for each step, with a point-by-point reply to their terms.

spec_fields.label: What do you need a plan for?
options: Win plan for a live deal
Shared close plan with the buyer
Supplier price talk or contract renewal
Payment plan for a customer who owes you

spec_fields.label: How many deals or accounts?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers one, up to five per job. A batch of renewals counts each customer.

spec_fields.label: What is happening
spec_fields.help: History, recent emails or call notes, what has been said so far.

spec_fields.label: The people involved
spec_fields.help: Names or roles, what each does, and what you know about each.

spec_fields.label: The numbers and terms on the table
spec_fields.help: Price, volume, contract length, amount owed, current terms.

spec_fields.label: What would a good outcome be?
What you can and cannot offer
spec_fields.help: Your walk-away point and things you could give.

spec_fields.label: Key dates
spec_fields.help: Deadlines, renewal date, board meeting, quarter end.

spec_fields.label: How you like to come across

rubric.text: Every person, number, date and term comes from the brief, and the numbers add up.
rubric.pass_rule: No name, role, price, discount, date, contract term or fact about the other side appears unless the brief gives it; guesses about what someone cares about are labelled 'likely' and tied to a note; any payment schedule adds up to the amount in the brief.

rubric.text: Goal, walk-away point and possible trades are stated.
rubric.pass_rule: States the goal, a walk-away or fallback (from the brief, or marked for the buyer to set), and at least three trades or offers ranked by cost to give and value to the other side, all inside the limits in the brief.

rubric.text: A dated action plan with owners.
rubric.pass_rule: Lists next steps in order, each with an owner (name or role from the brief) and a date or week, ending at the outcome in the brief; every date falls before any deadline the brief gives.

rubric.text: Messages or talking points are ready to send or say.
rubric.pass_rule: Each step that involves contact has a message or talking points under 150 words for the right person, using the plan's numbers; for counter-offers every term in their message gets a reply.

rubric.text: Honest tactics and plain words.
rubric.pass_rule: No false deadlines, bluffs about rival offers the brief does not mention, threats or pressure; plain words; for each account in a batch the plan is clearly separated.

baseline_prompt: You are a deal and negotiation coach for small businesses. Using only my notes below, write a plan for this one deal, account, renewal, at-risk customer, stuck issue or negotiation. Sum up the situation. Map the people involved and what each likely cares about, marking guesses as likely. List the risks. State my goal, my walk-away point and at least three things I could trade, ranked by what they cost me and what they are worth to the other side. Describe their likely position. Give a dated action plan with an owner for each step, ending at the outcome I want, and write the message or talking points for each step. If I pasted their terms, reply to each point. Keep every number and date from my notes, check any payment schedule adds up, and use honest tactics only. Not legal or financial advice.
not_for: Negotiating, calling or sending messages for you
Deceptive, high-pressure or threatening tactics
Legal advice on contracts, debt recovery or insolvency
Regulated advice on loans, insurance, debt or investments
A general price-talk or objection guide for all deals (see the objection handling guide job)
Logging in to your CRM, inbox or bank; paste notes instead
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Win plan for a 38,000 dollar a year deal with Halden Logistics for our route planning software. Champion: Maria (ops manager). Their CFO, Dan, has not joined a call. IT wants a security review. They are also trialling a rival. Notes from 4 calls pasted. Goal: signed by 15 December.

Supplier price talk. Our flour supplier, Millbrook, wants a 12% rise from January. We buy about 9 tonnes a month at 640 pounds a tonne, on 30-day terms, 4 years with them. A rival quoted 655 a tonne but needs 60-day notice to switch. Want a plan, a walk-away point and an opening email.

Save plan for our biggest client, Tilly's Garden Centres (3 sites, 2,100 dollars a month for our marketing retainer). Their new marketing head, Owen, said results are 'flat' and the contract ends 31 January. Results pasted. We can offer a free month of extra ads or a cheaper plan.

Renewal plans for 4 customers whose contracts end in Q1 (details pasted: plan, price, usage, last support issue, contacts). Customer 3 had a 2-day outage in August. We want to raise prices 6% where usage is up. Timeline from 90 days out and messages for each step.

A customer, Bayview Dental, owes us 7,200 dollars across three invoices for cleaning services, now 75 days late. The practice manager says cash is tight after a flood. We could accept 6 monthly payments. Need a kind payment plan offer with dates and what happens if a date is missed.

Counter-offer reply. Buyer at Norcross Hotels sent their terms for 140 bed frames: 18% discount, 90-day payment, free delivery to 5 sites, penalty of 2% per late week. Our list price is 310 each, we can do 8% off and 45 days. Their message is pasted. Reply point by point and plan the next call.

demand_sources.note: Consulting cost guide: small businesses pay on average $2,500 to $7,500 per consulting project, with boutique firms charging up to $300 an hour.

title: Plan for one marketing channel, paid or organic
summary: A plan for one channel: Google, Meta, LinkedIn or TikTok ads, TikTok Shop, Pinterest, YouTube, email, Reddit, your own community, Amazon or AI search.
deliverable: Channel goal and fit; set-up in the channel's own structure (campaigns, ad groups and keywords, audiences, boards, series or a send calendar); budget split; week-by-week or month-by-month actions; content or creative needs; a launch checklist; the numbers to track; and the first tests.

spec_fields.label: Which channel?
options: Meta ads (Facebook and Instagram), including retargeting
AI search (being named by AI assistants)

spec_fields.label: How long should the plan run?
What you sell and the price
Who buys

Risk assessment and daily inspection checklists for our garden centre's loading yard in Ohio: forklift (1), pallet racking, customers' cars nearby, staff lifting compost bags (25 kg). Two near misses with the forklift this year. Yard lead: Carla.

title: Retention and win-back plan

deliverable: Where people leave, from your data; warning signs and actions for quiet customers; a journey from joining or first order to renewal with the message for each step; a cancel flow with pause, skip or swap and an easy exit; win-back, reactivation and referral messages with who to contact first; a follow-up plan for unhappy customers; and the numbers to track.

Past client reactivation and referral asks

rubric.text: Where people leave is read from the buyer's data.
rubric.pass_rule: Names the points where people leave or go quiet using figures from the brief (counts or rates with the sum shown), or says which data is missing; warning signs use behaviours the brief says it can track.

rubric.text: Only the buyer's numbers, offers and reasons.
rubric.pass_rule: No churn rate, cancel reason, discount, offer, customer name or result appears unless it is in the brief; any expected effect is labelled as a guess, not promised.

rubric.pass_rule: Any cancel flow offers pause, skip or swap once and then lets the person cancel in no more than two more steps; there are no guilt-trip lines, hidden buttons or false deadlines; messages go only to people who have not opted out.

Messages to people who opted out or never agreed to hear from you
Sending the messages for you, or logging in to your email, CRM or billing tools
Guaranteed cuts in churn

Full email flows built in your email tool (see the post-purchase email flow job)
Customer emails, phone numbers, card numbers or passwords in the brief

Paycor tracker of state pay transparency laws: states including Colorado, New York (4 or more staff) and New Jersey (10 or more) require pay ranges in job ads.

title: Lead magnet and funnel plan with copy
summary: A free offer that fits your buyer, the path from sign-up to first sale, and the copy for the sign-up page, follow-up emails and first paid step.
deliverable: Three lead magnet ideas scored for fit, with the best one outlined (or written in full if short); a funnel map in words with the goal and exit for each step; sign-up page text; three to five follow-up emails; the first paid step; and for quizzes or workshops, the questions, results and emails or the outline and reminders.

spec_fields.label: What do you need?
options: Pick and outline a lead magnet
Full funnel: free offer, page, emails and first paid step

spec_fields.label: Who you want to attract
spec_fields.help: Who they are and the problem they want solved.

spec_fields.label: What you could give away
spec_fields.help: Know-how, templates, a checklist, a short call, a sample.

spec_fields.label: Your current sign-up flow and results
spec_fields.help: Pages, emails, list size, sign-up and sales rates.

spec_fields.label: Proof we may use
spec_fields.help: Results, quotes, numbers. Only these will be used.

spec_fields.label: Email and page tools you use
Tone and voice
spec_fields.help: A few words, or paste a sample of your writing.

rubric.text: The free offer solves one real part of the buyer's problem and leads to the paid offer.
rubric.pass_rule: Names the free offer, why it fits the buyer's problem from the brief and how it leads to the main offer; when asked to pick one, three ideas are scored on the same criteria before the choice.

rubric.text: Each step has a goal and an exit.
rubric.pass_rule: The map lists every step in order (page, thank-you step, each email, offer) and gives each a goal, the action wanted and what happens if the person does not act.

rubric.text: Page text and emails are written and ready to paste.
rubric.pass_rule: The sign-up page has headline, bullets, form ask and button; there are 3 to 5 follow-up emails, each with subject line, body under 200 words and one call to action; quizzes add questions, result types and a result page and email per result; workshops add a timed outline and reminder emails.

rubric.text: No made-up proof, results, numbers or scarcity.
rubric.pass_rule: No testimonial, result, subscriber count, price, deadline or limited number appears unless it is in the brief; no fake countdowns or 'only 3 left' lines.

rubric.text: Plain words and opt-in respected.
rubric.pass_rule: Copy uses plain words and short sentences; the sign-up page says what people will get by email; nothing suggests emailing people who did not sign up.

baseline_prompt: You are a funnel strategist and copywriter for small businesses. Using only my facts below, plan a lead magnet and funnel. Give three free-offer ideas scored on fit with my buyer's problem, speed to use, link to my main offer and effort to make, and outline the best one (write it in full if it is a short checklist or one-page guide). Map the funnel in words: sign-up page, thank-you step, each email and the offer, with the goal and the exit for each step. Write the sign-up page text, three to five follow-up emails with subject lines, and a small first paid step that leads to my main offer. For a quiz, write the questions, result types and a result page and email per result. For a free workshop, write a timed outline, the sign-up page and reminder emails, with a soft offer at the end. No invented proof, fake urgency or false scarcity.
not_for: Building pages, quizzes or automations in your tools, or logging in to them
Fake urgency or invented scarcity
Emailing people who did not opt in
Guaranteed lead or sales numbers
Health, money or legal promises that need regulated advice
Long lead magnets such as an ebook or course (see the long-form guide job)
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Pick and outline a lead magnet for my bookkeeping service for UK tradespeople (electricians, plumbers). They hate paperwork and fear the tax return. Main offer: 95 pounds a month bookkeeping. I could give away my receipt-sorting system and a list of costs they can claim. Score three ideas.

Full funnel for my interior design e-course 'Small Rooms, Big Ideas' (149 dollars). Buyers: renters in small flats. Current flow: Instagram bio link straight to the sales page, 0.6% buy. I want a free offer, sign-up page, 4 emails and a small paid first step at about 19 dollars.

Quiz funnel for our running shoe shop: 'Which trail shoe suits you?'. 6 to 8 questions, 4 result types (we stock 14 trail shoes, list pasted), a result page and a follow-up email for each. Goal: book a free gait check in store.

Free 45-minute workshop funnel for my coaching for new team leads in hospitality. Teach one thing: running a 10-minute pre-shift briefing. Sign-up page, 3 reminder emails, outline with timings, and a soft offer at the end for my 6-week programme (450 pounds).

Funnel map only for our B2B cleaning company. We get website visitors from Google but few quote requests. Steps today: home page, quote form, nothing else. Map a better path with a free offer (maybe a cleaning checklist for office managers), the goal and exit for each step.

demand_sources.note: AWAI article on funnel pricing: copywriters charged $5,000 to $10,000 for a basic funnel of lead magnet, offer page, upsell and follow-up emails (2015 figures).
2026 email copywriter rate guide: welcome emails $50 to $150 each, nurture emails $75 to $200, and $400 to $600 for a starter five-email welcome sequence.

title: Book proposal, chapter outline or sample chapter
summary: A nonfiction book proposal for agents or publishers, a chapter-by-chapter outline, or one chapter drafted from your notes in your voice.
deliverable: A proposal with overview, the reader, comparable titles you name, your platform, chapter summaries and a marketing plan; or title options, the book's promise and an outline of 10 to 14 chapters with purpose, key points and stories; or a 3,000 to 5,000 word chapter in your voice with claims needing a source flagged.

spec_fields.label: How many documents?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers one, up to two per job. A proposal plus a sample chapter counts as two.

spec_fields.label: Your book idea and its promise to readers
Your notes, stories or transcripts
spec_fields.help: Talks, posts, client stories, interview transcripts. Stories used come only from here.

spec_fields.label: Comparable titles
spec_fields.help: Title, author and year. We only use the ones you give.

spec_fields.label: Your platform
spec_fields.help: List size, followers, talks, clients, media. Only these numbers are used.

spec_fields.label: Which chapter to draft, and length
spec_fields.help: For a sample chapter. Default is about 4,000 words.

rubric.text: The document has every part its type needs.
rubric.pass_rule: A proposal has overview, the reader, comparable titles, author platform, a summary for every chapter and a marketing plan (or follows the guidelines in the brief); an outline has title options, the promise and 10 to 14 chapters each with purpose, key points, stories and a link to the next; a chapter is 3,000 to 5,000 words or the length asked.

rubric.text: No made-up stories, studies, quotes, comparable titles or platform numbers.
rubric.pass_rule: Every story, client example, statistic, study, quote, comparable title and follower or sales number is from the brief; claims that need a source are marked [source needed]; no sales figures are given for comparable titles unless supplied.

rubric.text: It sounds like the author.
rubric.pass_rule: Uses the author's own phrases and stories from the notes, keeps first person if the notes use it, matches any writing sample, and avoids filler such as 'in today's fast-paced world'.

rubric.text: A clear promise and a logical flow.
rubric.pass_rule: States the book's promise to the reader in one or two sentences near the start; each chapter or section builds on the one before; no point is repeated across two chapters.

rubric.text: Plain, readable prose.
rubric.pass_rule: Most sentences are under 25 words, jargon is explained, and headings make the structure clear at a glance.

baseline_prompt: You are a nonfiction book coach and ghostwriter. Using only my idea, notes, comparable titles and platform below, write the document I chose. For a book proposal, write an overview with the book's promise, who the reader is, the comparable titles I name and how my book differs, my platform with only the numbers I give, a summary for every chapter and a marketing plan, following any agent or publisher guidelines I paste. For an outline, give title options, the core promise and 10 to 14 chapters, each with its purpose, key points, the stories from my notes to use and how it leads to the next. For a sample chapter, write 3,000 to 5,000 words in my voice from my notes. Do not invent stories, studies, quotes, comparable titles or numbers, and mark any claim that needs a source as [source needed]. Keep the prose plain and readable.
not_for: Finding an agent or publisher, or sending queries for you
Writing a whole book in one job
Invented stories, studies, quotes, comparable titles or sales figures
Medical, legal or financial advice stated as fact without your expert review
Novels and other fiction
Editing, formatting, cover design or publishing
Passwords, logins, card numbers or bank details in the brief

sample_briefs.text: Book proposal for 'The Quiet Shop', a book for independent retailers on growing without discounting. I have run a hardware store in Vermont for 22 years and write a newsletter with 8,400 subscribers. Comparable titles I chose: 'Profit First' (Michalowicz, 2014) and 'The E-Myth Revisited' (Gerber, 1995). Notes and 14 newsletter essays pasted.

Chapter-by-chapter outline for a book on hiring your first five employees, for owners of trades businesses. Transcripts of 6 talks I gave and 30 client stories (anonymised) pasted. Reader: plumbers, electricians and builders with 1 to 3 staff.

Sample chapter, chapter 3 'The 20-minute weekly money meeting', about 4,000 words, for my book on money habits for creative freelancers. My notes, two podcast transcripts and a writing sample pasted. First person, warm and direct. Flag anything that needs a source.

Proposal plus sample chapter (2 documents) for a book about running a calm restaurant kitchen, by me, a chef-owner of two restaurants in Leeds. Agent guidelines pasted (proposal under 30 pages, sample chapter required). Platform: 31,000 Instagram followers, regular BBC Radio Leeds guest. Notes pasted.

demand_sources.note: Reedsy's guide to ghostwriting costs says a book proposal costs between $1,000 and $10,000.
Freelance Writer Search: ASJA members report average fees of $5,000 to $20,000 for book proposals.
